title: Orthographic grids always visible in overdraw & lighting display modes
body:
### Tested versions

v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee]

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.5768) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1185G7 @ 3.00GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

**Flashing/flickering image warning:** please be advised that this issue is about a visual disturbance in the Godot editor that can include rapid flashing/flickering.

The grids in the 3D viewport are shown in the overdraw & lighting display modes.
The most pressing issue with this is the visual disturbance when rotating/orbiting in orthographic view.
Static view angles (particularly non-axis aligned) are difficult to use because of the visual noise added by the grid.
In the other main display modes, the grid fades out as the view is rotated off-axis.

This makes orthographic projection very difficult to use without disabling (hiding) the grid.

- With a perspective projection the issue is also present, but is less disruptive.
- Tested in Compatibility and Forward+

I've attached a video demonstrating this. It's worth noting that the video compression clearly had a hard time with the capture and resulted in a somewhat less intense effect.

The attached **video contains flashing/flickering**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab71ecb1-95f0-4ab8-a76f-d996f4421763

### Steps to reproduce

In an empty project with default editor settings,
1. Enter the 3D viewport
2. Switch to Orthographic mode
3. Rotate (orbit) the view and note that grid/s are only visible when near perpendicular to the view direction. The grid fades out smoothly as the view is rotated away from the axis.
4. Enable the 'Display Overdraw' viewport option
5. Rotate (orbit) the view and note that all three grids are visible regardless of view rotation.
